bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in generic_unpack (src/lib/OpenEXRCore/unpack.c): while unpacking/decoding image data (via exr_decoding_run / readCoreScanlinePart), generic_unpack performs an out-of-bounds read of 4 bytes past a heap-allocated buffer. This insufficient bounds checking / incorrect buffer sizing can cause crashes, memory corruption and may enable information disclosure or further exploitation when parsing crafted OpenEXR files.
bug_description.normalized: A crafted OpenEXR scanline chunk makes a sampled channel contribute more sampled rows than the vulnerable decoder counts with integer division. `compute_chunk_unpack_size` and `internal_coding_fill_channel_info` both reduce the chunk's sampled-row count with `height / y_sampling`, `exr_decoding_run` allocates `decode->unpacked_buffer` to the smaller `chunk.unpacked_size`, and `generic_unpack` still consumes the additional sampled row selected by the modulo gate, leading `unaligned_load32` to read 4 bytes past the heap buffer.

source.value_from: OpenEXR header channel list parsed from the testcase file
source.description: While deriving unpacked bytes for a scanline chunk, project code first consumes the file-controlled channel `y_sampling` to choose the sampled-line sizing path for this channel.

root_cause.description: For sampled channels in multi-line scanline chunks, the vulnerable code derives channel bytes from `height / y_sampling`. That floors the sampled-row count instead of counting sampled scanlines relative to `start_y`, so the chunk's unpacked byte size is smaller than the data `generic_unpack` later consumes.

sink.description: `generic_unpack` reaches the extra sampled row and executes `UNPACK_SAMPLES(w)`, which for 4-byte channel types calls `unaligned_load32` on `srcbuffer` after the undersized heap buffer has already been exhausted.

parser_admitted.description: The testcase has already passed OpenEXR parsing and header validation; `exrcheck` is now iterating an admitted scanline part and querying concrete chunk metadata for the requested scanline.

tainted_value_origin.description: Channel sampling values parsed from the OpenEXR header directly control both chunk byte sizing and which rows the unpack loop later treats as sampled rows.

coarse_trace.summary: `exrcheck` walks an admitted scanline part, reads chunk metadata for the chosen scanline, and then invokes the decode pipeline for that chunk.
Chunk reading computes `cinfo->unpacked_size` from `compute_chunk_unpack_size`, using the channel sampling factors and chunk geometry.
Decoder channel setup copies the same sampled-channel geometry into `decode->channels`, including a too-small sampled-row count in `decc->height`.
The decode pipeline allocates `decode->unpacked_buffer` using the underestimated `chunk.unpacked_size` and then calls `generic_unpack`.

`generic_unpack` still visits the additional sampled row selected by the modulo test, advances `srcbuffer` through more sampled-row data than the allocation covered, and performs the observed 4-byte out-of-bounds read.

fine_trace.note: While sizing this scanline chunk, the code reads the header-controlled channel `y_sampling` and takes the sampled-channel sizing path for that channel.
For a multi-line chunk, the code reduces channel bytes with `height / y_sampling`, flooring the sampled-row count instead of counting sampled scanlines from `start_y`.
The truncated per-channel byte count is accumulated into `unpacksize` and stored as the chunk's authoritative unpacked byte size.
Decoder channel setup repeats the same floor division for sampled channels, so `decc->height` records too few sampled rows for this chunk relative to its real sampled scanlines.
The same decoder descriptor also keeps the original sampling period in `decc->y_samples`, which the unpack loop later uses only to decide whether an absolute row is sampled.

Because packed and unpacked sizes differ, the decode pipeline allocates `decode->unpacked_buffer` with `decode->chunk.unpacked_size` bytes, so the heap object inherits the undersized allocation caused by the floored sampled-row count. The ASan allocation stack reports this path through `internal_decode_alloc_buffer`.
On the crashing iteration, the current absolute row satisfies the sampling-period test, so this predicate admits that row for unpacking. The modulo check is only the row-selection gate.

Each sampled row that passes the gate consumes one row of source bytes. Because allocation sizing counted only the floored sampled-row total while unpacking still reaches this additional sampled row, the cumulative `srcbuffer` advances run past the bytes reserved in `decode->unpacked_buffer`.

`UNPACK_SAMPLES(w)` performs the next pixel reads from `srcbuffer`; for FLOAT and UINT-sized elements it calls `unaligned_load32`. After the extra sampled-row consumption has exhausted the shorter heap object, this becomes the observed 4-byte out-of-bounds read.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The patch replaces the vulnerable `height / y_sampling` undercount in both `compute_chunk_unpack_size` and `internal_coding_fill_channel_info` with `compute_sampled_lines(...)`, removing the allocation-versus-consumption mismatch that this trace describes.

format.name: OpenEXR scanline image
format.contract: The file must be accepted as an OpenEXR scanline part and include at least one channel with `y_sampling > 1` where the triggered chunk contains one more sampled scanline than vulnerable floor-division `height / y_sampling` accounts for. That makes `cinfo->unpacked_size` too small for the sampled-row bytes `generic_unpack` consumes before the observed 4-byte out-of-bounds read.
